symptom: `alter entity M.E add event handler on before commit call M.Second($currentObject)` failed with "event handler already exists for Before Commit" when the entity already had a Before Commit handler, while `create or modify entity` with two `on before commit` clauses stored both. The same key hid two quieter defects: `add event handler if not exists … call M.New` printed "already exists, skipping" for a microflow never wired, and `drop event handler on before commit` removed whichever handler was stored first
cause: ALTER ENTITY keyed a handler on (Moment, Event) alone, in both arms. A handler's identity is (Moment, Event, Microflow): Mendix allows several per event, and the DROP grammar had no way to name the microflow at all
file: `mdl/executor/cmd_entities.go` (`matchEventHandlers`, `storedHandlerMicroflow`, both event-handler arms of execAlterEntity), `mdl/grammar/domains/MDLDomainModel.g4` (`(CALL qualifiedName)?` on DROP EVENT HANDLER), `mdl/visitor/visitor_entity.go`; tests `mdl/executor/alter_entity_event_handlers_test.go`, `mdl/visitor/drop_event_handler_call_test.go`; repro `mdl-examples/bug-tests/alter-entity-1540-second-event-handler.mdl`
insight: When ADD's duplicate key is too coarse, look at DROP and the IF [NOT] EXISTS guards on the same key: all three were wrong, and two of them silently (a skip notice for a handler never added; the first-stored handler dropped). Once ADD can create two, a bare DROP is ambiguous, so it is refused and names the candidates rather than taking the first (the mutator-addressing rule). The validity claim was measured, not assumed, on 11.12.4 with three projects: two Before Commit handlers via ALTER = 0 errors; the same via the OLD binary's create or modify = 0 errors; a void-returning Before Commit handler = CE7247 (the control that shows mx check looks at handlers at all). The same microflow twice on one event is ALSO 0 errors, so ADD's remaining refusal of an exact duplicate is mxcli's re-run guard (it would run twice per commit), not a Mendix rule; say that in the comment rather than letting it read as one. Wrong turn to skip: renaming a copied project's .mpr breaks mx with StorageMprNameDiscrepancyException, which looks like a model failure
